subject: Annual prepay: invoice phasing, receipts gating and drawdown logistics
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annual prepay: invoice phasing, receipts gating and drawdown logistics

Hi Marta —

Following our call this morning, I put together a proposal for phasing the annual prepay and the operational steps wed need on your side to trigger drawdowns. High level: we can split the committed spend into an initial deposit + staged invoices over the year with automated usage top-ups. This reduces cash burden for Acme while keeping predictable lane for Redwood.

Key items in the attached draft:
- Initial deposit: 30% of committed amount (invoice on signature)
- Phased invoices: 4 quarterly invoices (25%/25%/10%/10%) aligned to product rollout milestones
- Usage-triggered drawdowns: monthly top-ups billed when usage crosses threshold (3% of committed per threshold)
- Receipt gating: finance needs a scanned supplier receipt / PO uploaded to the payments portal within 7 days of invoice to trigger ledger acceptance and VAT processing

Questions for you so we can finalize:
1) Will Acme provide a single legal entity for billing or multiple EU subsidiaries?
2) Do you have a preferred PO number pattern and internal remit contact for the portal?
3) Do you need us to split invoices by country for VAT purposes or would a single invoice with VAT breakdown suffice?

Attached: 2028-06-12_Acme_Invoice_Draft.pdf (invoice schedule + line items).

If that structure looks good, Ill loop in Finance (Kimberly) to pin bank wiring and VAT-form requirements, and Ops (Laura) for acceptance criteria and rollout gating.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0198

[Attachment: 2028-06-12_Acme_Invoice_Draft.pdf (PDF, 122KB)]

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual prepay: invoice phasing, receipts gating and drawdown logistics

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary and draft, that format looks promising. A couple of clarifications from procurement here so we can route internally:

- VAT: Acme has both a UK-registered entity and an NL entity; procurement prefers country-level invoicing so tax can be posted to the correct ledger. Will Redwood produce invoices split by legal entity if we provide VAT ids?
- PO: Procurement requires a signed PO before the initial deposit invoice is processed on our side; PO number will follow the pattern ACME-RW-YYYYMM-XXXX.
- Receipts gating: well need the invoice to include a clear VAT breakdown and the Redwood VAT/trading registration number to let AP accept it.

I can get you the NL VAT id by end of day Friday and initiate the PO request. Two asks: can you (1) confirm wiring details and (2) confirm whether the quarterly phasing can be converted to monthly micro-invoices in months where usage spikes? That helps smoothing internal forecasting.

Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
marta.ruiz@acme-analytics.com | +44 20 7946 0123

Subject: Re: Annual prepay: invoice phasing, receipts gating and drawdown logistics

Hi all — quick finance read and recommended ops pattern from our side: 

Proposed billing cadence (finance-preferred):
1) Initial deposit invoice (30%) — due on receipt; requires signed PO and remit confirmation
2) Monthly micro-invoices as usage warrants (usage threshold at 50% of monthly allotment triggers a top-up invoice)
3) Quarterly balancing invoices (to reconcile committed vs usage)
4) Annual true-up invoice (final reconciliation and credit/overage settle)

VAT / tax handling:
- If Acme provides valid EU VAT ids per legal entity, we will issue entity-specific invoices with reverse-charge where applicable.
- If not, Redwood will invoice with UK VAT applied where service is supplied to UK legal entity.
- We need copies of VAT registration (VIES check acceptable) before we remove VAT from invoices.

Receipt gating + evidence:
- AP requires: PO#, invoice PDF, and one of: supplier contract reference OR portal-uploaded receipt within 7 calendar days.
- If evidence not uploaded within 7 days, ledger acceptance is delayed and access to committed capacity may be temporarily suspended until resolved.

Wiring and remits:
- Please use finance_wire_instructions.txt (attached) for bank details and reference formatting. For ACH to US accounts we require beneficiary name and invoice number in the reference.

Ill also flag Treasury for a pre-authorize step for initial deposit > $250k.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

[Attachment: finance_wire_instructions.txt (PLAINTEXT)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual prepay: invoice phasing, receipts gating and drawdown logistics

Marta —

Appreciate the quick turn. Per Kims notes, we can accommodate:
- Split invoices by legal entity if you supply VAT ids and remit entities (please attach in reply)
- Well issue the initial deposit invoice on signature and hold the monthly micro-invoice automation behind the usage thresholds you requested

Operational checklist (what we need from Acme to start):
1) Signed PO (ACME format) for initial deposit
2) VAT ids per entity (NL/UK) to determine invoice routing
3) Primary remit contact and preferred invoice recipient email for each legal entity

Acceptance + gating: once an invoice is issued, AP uploads the invoice PDF + PO to the Redwood Payments Portal (link below). Upload within 7 days = automatic ledger acceptance and VAT routing. Failure to upload = manual review and hold.

Payment portal: https://app.redwood-inference.com/payments/portal/ACME-12345
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/objects/deal/ACME-RW-2028-Q2-17

Attached: updated phasing schedule (2028-06-12_invoice-phasing-schedule.pdf) with the monthly micro-invoice example and sample ledger tagging fields. Ive also included a sample invoice reference we recommend: ACME-RW-INV-20280612-<PO#>.

If youre good with that, I can send the DocuSign with the payment schedule and have legal include the PO acceptance clause.

Best —
Jonas

[Attachment: 2028-06-12_invoice-phasing-schedule.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: invoice phasing — ops notes and recommendations

Internal note (not for customer):

Jonas / Kim — my operational recommendations before we send the DocuSign: 
- Add a rollover credit clause: unused committed credits can roll forward one quarter only; after that they expire. This avoids month-end reconciliation backlog.
- Auto-charge fallback: if AP does not upload receipt within 14 days, send two reminder emails; if still unresolved after 30 days, auto-charge to the saved payment method provided by procurement (we need procurement approval for auto-charge in DocuSign).
- Treasury: confirm pre-authorize threshold for initial deposits > $250k (Kim, can you confirm?)
- Tagging: include a CSV-friendly meta field on each invoice (legal_entity, PO, project_code) to speed bookkeeping imports.

Id also like to ensure Legal adds a short SLA for ledger acceptance time (48 hours after evidence receipt) so customers have predictable expectations.

LMK and Ill fold these into the envelope before sending.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Account Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Thanks — this looks workable. Procurement will raise the PO (ACME-RW-202806-0021) and I will upload the NL VAT id and remit contacts by next Tuesday. A couple of small asks: 

1) Please break the first quarterly invoice into 3 monthly micro-invoices for July/August/September (we have seasonality and need the flexibility).
2) We prefer the rollover credit to roll forward two quarters instead of one — will that be acceptable?

Once we receive the DocuSign Ill get procurement to sign and trigger the PO. Please include the DocuSign link and the final invoice PDFs in the envelope.

Marta
